FINAL IVX REGISTRATION + SIGN-IN CLOSEOUT
100 EXACT EXECUTION STEPS — COMPLETE ONE BY ONE

DO NOT RETURN A GENERAL REPORT.
DO NOT SKIP STEPS.
DO NOT MARK 100% COMPLETE UNTIL EVERY REQUIRED LIVE TEST PASSES.

CURRENT STATUS:

Already working:
- Auth user creation
- Member row creation
- Profile creation
- Investment-interest creation
- Duplicate prevention
- Database constraints
- RLS
- Member login API
- Owner login
- CloudFront invalidation
- Registration metrics

Still incomplete:
- Production SMTP
- Real confirmation-email delivery
- Real forgot-password delivery
- Password-reset completion
- Session persistence on real devices
- Samsung Browser QA
- Android Chrome QA
- iPhone Safari QA
- Desktop browser QA
- Full live registration-to-login proof

OBJECTIVE:

A new visitor must be able to:

Landing page
→ Sign Up
→ Receive verification email
→ Verify email
→ Continue to Step 4
→ Log out
→ Sign in again
→ Close and reopen the app/browser
→ Remain signed in
→ Reset password
→ Sign in with new password
→ Access only the correct member routes

Owner must continue to access owner-only routes.

==================================================
SECTION A — FREEZE THE CURRENT STATE
==================================================

1. Record the current GitHub HEAD SHA.

2. Record the current Render runtime SHA.

3. Confirm GitHub HEAD equals Render runtime SHA.

4. Record the current APK version and version code.

5. Record the production Supabase project reference.

6. Record the current CloudFront distribution ID.

7. Record the current landing-page index.html ETag.

8. Record the current ivx-invest.js checksum.

9. Record the current ivx-portal.js checksum.

10. Save the current registration metrics as the before-state baseline.

==================================================
SECTION B — SMTP CONFIGURATION
==================================================

11. Open the Supabase project used by production IVX.

12. Open Authentication settings.

13. Open SMTP settings.

14. Confirm the current SMTP host is empty.

15. Confirm the current SMTP port is empty.

16. Confirm the current SMTP username is empty.

17. Confirm the current SMTP password is empty.

18. Select the owner-approved SMTP provider.

19. Use an owner-controlled IVX sender domain.

20. Create the sender address, for example:
no-reply@ivxholding.com

21. Configure the SMTP host.

22. Configure the SMTP port.

23. Configure the SMTP username.

24. Configure the SMTP password.

25. Configure the sender name:
IVX Holdings

26. Configure the sender email.

27. Enable TLS or the provider’s required secure transport.

28. Add the SPF DNS record.

29. Add the DKIM DNS record.

30. Add the DMARC DNS record.

31. Wait for DNS propagation.

32. Verify SPF passes.

33. Verify DKIM passes.

34. Verify DMARC is detected.

35. Save the Supabase SMTP configuration.

36. Send one test confirmation email.

37. Send one test password-reset email.

38. Confirm both emails arrive.

39. Confirm neither email lands in spam during the primary test.

40. Record the SMTP provider, sender domain, delivery timestamp, and proof.

Do not expose SMTP credentials in the final report.

==================================================
SECTION C — AUTH REDIRECT URLS
==================================================

41. Verify the production site URL is:
https://ivxholding.com

42. Verify the member portal callback URL exists.

43. Verify the password-reset callback route exists.

44. Verify the email-confirmation callback route exists.

45. Add all approved production redirect URLs to Supabase Auth.

46. Remove obsolete Rork, Vercel, local, or staging callback URLs unless still intentionally required.

47. Confirm Android deep-link configuration if the app opens verification links.

48. Confirm iOS universal-link configuration if available.

49. Confirm an invalid redirect URL is rejected.

50. Confirm the correct redirect returns the user to the intended IVX screen.

==================================================
SECTION D — SIGN-UP CODE QA
==================================================

51. Find the landing-page sign-up form handler.

52. Confirm it uses the canonical production Supabase configuration.

53. Confirm it does not create a separate duplicate Supabase client.

54. Confirm email is trimmed.

55. Confirm email is lowercased.

56. Confirm password characters are preserved exactly.

57. Confirm password is never lowercased.

58. Confirm password is never written to logs.

59. Confirm the service-role key is not present in the browser bundle.

60. Confirm the Create Account button disables immediately after one tap.

61. Confirm double-tapping creates only one request ID.

62. Confirm the request ID is sent to the backend.

63. Confirm the backend returns the same result for a repeated request ID.

64. Confirm exactly one Auth user is created.

65. Confirm exactly one members row is created.

66. Confirm exactly one profiles row is created.

67. Confirm exactly one landing_investments row is created.

68. Confirm all four records are linked to the same user.

69. Confirm the selected deal ID is preserved.

70. Confirm the selected investment amount is preserved.

==================================================
SECTION E — EMAIL CONFIRMATION
==================================================

71. Create a new disposable production QA email address.

72. Start registration from the public landing page.

73. Complete Steps 1 and 2.

74. Complete the Sign Up form.

75. Submit once.

76. Confirm the UI displays:
Check your email

77. Confirm the verification email arrives.

78. Confirm the sender is the official IVX sender.

79. Confirm the email contains the correct IVX branding.

80. Open the verification link.

81. Confirm the link returns to the correct IVX production URL.

82. Confirm the Supabase email-confirmed timestamp is updated.

83. Confirm the member session is established or the user is asked to sign in.

84. Confirm the selected deal and amount are restored.

85. Confirm Step 4 opens successfully.

==================================================
SECTION F — MEMBER SIGN-IN
==================================================

86. Log out the newly created member.

87. Sign in with the correct email and password.

88. Confirm HTTP 200 or the correct Supabase success response.

89. Confirm the correct member profile loads.

90. Confirm the correct member role loads.

91. Confirm the user cannot access Owner Dashboard.

92. Confirm the user cannot access Admin Hub.

93. Confirm the user cannot access Variables.

94. Confirm protected owner APIs return 401 or 403 for the member.

95. Enter the wrong password.

96. Confirm the wrong password is rejected.

97. Enter the email with different capitalization.

98. Confirm normalized email login still works.

99. Tap Sign In twice rapidly.

100. Confirm only one login request is processed.

==================================================
SECTION G — SESSION PERSISTENCE
==================================================

101. Sign in successfully.

102. Refresh the browser.

103. Confirm the user remains signed in.

104. Close the browser tab.

105. Reopen the IVX site.

106. Confirm the session restores.

107. Background the browser for one minute.

108. Return to the browser.

109. Confirm the session remains valid.

110. Disable the network.

111. Reopen the member page.

112. Confirm the app shows a controlled offline state.

113. Restore the network.

114. Confirm the session refreshes automatically.

115. Confirm no infinite authentication loop occurs.

116. Confirm no duplicate session is created.

117. Confirm the refresh token rotates according to Supabase behavior.

118. Log out.

119. Confirm protected member data is cleared from the UI.

120. Confirm the user remains logged out after refresh.

==================================================
SECTION H — PASSWORD RESET
==================================================

121. Open Forgot Password.

122. Enter the member email.

123. Submit once.

124. Confirm a neutral success response is shown.

125. Confirm the response does not reveal whether unrelated emails exist.

126. Confirm the reset email arrives.

127. Open the reset link.

128. Confirm the reset link opens the official IVX reset route.

129. Enter a new strong password.

130. Submit the new password.

131. Confirm the password update succeeds.

132. Attempt login with the old password.

133. Confirm the old password is rejected.

134. Attempt login with the new password.

135. Confirm the new password succeeds.

136. Reuse the same reset link.

137. Confirm the reused link is rejected.

138. Test an expired reset link.

139. Confirm the expired link shows a safe recovery option.

140. Confirm no password value appears in logs, analytics, or traces.

==================================================
SECTION I — OWNER AUTHENTICATION
==================================================

141. Confirm the canonical owner user exists in production Supabase.

142. Confirm the owner email is verified.

143. Confirm the owner is not banned or disabled.

144. Confirm the owner role is stored server-side.

145. Sign in as owner.

146. Confirm Owner Dashboard opens.

147. Confirm Admin Hub opens.

148. Confirm Variables opens.

149. Confirm IVX IA Chat opens.

150. Confirm owner-only APIs return HTTP 200.

151. Log out.

152. Sign in again.

153. Close and reopen the app/browser.

154. Confirm owner-session persistence.

155. Enter the wrong owner password.

156. Confirm rejection.

157. Sign in as an ordinary member.

158. Attempt the owner route.

159. Confirm 401 or 403.

160. Confirm MFA remains optional and OFF by default.

==================================================
SECTION J — PARTIAL-ACCOUNT REPAIR
==================================================

161. Create a controlled test where Auth exists but the member row is missing.

162. Run the repair flow.

163. Confirm the missing member row is created.

164. Confirm no second Auth user is created.

165. Create a test where member exists but interest row is missing.

166. Run the repair flow.

167. Confirm the missing interest row is created.

168. Create a test where the client times out after backend completion.

169. Retry using the same request ID.

170. Confirm the existing result is returned.

171. Create a duplicate simultaneous submission test.

172. Confirm unique constraints prevent duplicates.

173. Confirm the user receives one final success result.

174. Confirm the metrics record only one completed registration.

175. Confirm every partial-repair action has a trace ID.

==================================================
SECTION K — ERROR QA
==================================================

176. Test invalid email.

177. Confirm INVALID_EMAIL appears.

178. Test weak password.

179. Confirm WEAK_PASSWORD appears.

180. Test an existing email.

181. Confirm the UI offers Log In and Forgot Password.

182. Test HTTP 429.

183. Confirm retry-after timing is respected.

184. Test HTTP 500.

185. Confirm a trace ID appears.

186. Test HTTP 502.

187. Confirm bounded retry occurs.

188. Test HTTP 503.

189. Confirm bounded retry occurs.

190. Test HTTP 504.

191. Confirm bounded retry occurs.

192. Test malformed JSON.

193. Confirm no page crash occurs.

194. Test missing configuration.

195. Confirm signup is disabled with a controlled message.

196. Test stale frontend assets.

197. Confirm the current asset marker is checked.

198. Confirm old responses cannot overwrite newer state.

199. Confirm all errors map to one documented error contract.

200. Confirm no generic “Service temporarily unavailable” appears without a trace ID.

==================================================
SECTION L — PHYSICAL DEVICE QA
==================================================

201. Install or open the current production IVX build on Android.

202. Open Samsung Browser.

203. Run a new member signup.

204. Confirm the keyboard does not hide the button.

205. Confirm autofill works.

206. Confirm password-manager input works.

207. Confirm back navigation preserves non-sensitive form data.

208. Confirm refresh recovery works.

209. Confirm email confirmation returns correctly.

210. Confirm sign-in works.

211. Confirm session persistence works.

212. Confirm password reset works.

213. Repeat the same flow in Android Chrome.

214. Repeat the same flow on iPhone Safari.

215. Repeat the same flow on desktop Chrome.

216. Repeat the same flow on desktop Safari.

217. Test on slow 4G.

218. Test network interruption.

219. Test background and return.

220. Record screenshots and timestamps for every platform.

Do not mark a device PASS unless the test was actually performed on that device.

==================================================
SECTION M — CLOUDFRONT AND PRODUCTION ASSETS
==================================================

221. Invalidate /index.html.

222. Invalidate the registration JavaScript file.

223. Invalidate the portal JavaScript file.

224. Wait for invalidation completion.

225. Fetch index.html from production.

226. Record ETag.

227. Record Last-Modified.

228. Record Content-Length.

229. Record SHA-256.

230. Fetch ivx-invest.js.

231. Record ETag and SHA-256.

232. Fetch ivx-portal.js.

233. Record ETag and SHA-256.

234. Confirm all assets contain the current release marker.

235. Confirm no stale cache hit returns the old registration code.

==================================================
SECTION N — AUTOMATED TESTS
==================================================

236. Run registration unit tests.

237. Run registration integration tests.

238. Run login tests.

239. Run owner-role tests.

240. Run member-role tests.

241. Run password-reset tests.

242. Run SMTP delivery tests.

243. Run idempotency tests.

244. Run partial-repair tests.

245. Run RLS tests.

246. Run cross-user access tests.

247. Run service-key-exposure scan.

248. Run password-log scan.

249. Run frontend TypeScript.

250. Run backend TypeScript.

251. Run lint.

252. Run production smoke tests.

253. Return exact pass, fail, and skip counts.

254. Do not hide skipped browser/device tests.

255. Fix every failing critical test before deployment.

==================================================
SECTION O — DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

256. Commit only registration/authentication-related changes.

257. Return the exact files changed.

258. Return the GitHub commit SHA.

259. Deploy the backend.

260. Return the Render deployment ID.

261. Wait for the deployment to become live.

262. Call /health.

263. Confirm HTTP 200.

264. Confirm runtime SHA equals GitHub SHA.

265. Deploy the landing assets.

266. Invalidate CloudFront.

267. Verify current assets again.

268. Build a new APK only if mobile authentication code changed.

269. Record APK version and version code.

270. Record APK SHA-256.

==================================================
SECTION P — FINAL LIVE CANARY
==================================================

271. Create one new disposable QA email.

272. Register from the live production landing page.

273. Verify email.

274. Confirm Auth user exists.

275. Confirm members row exists.

276. Confirm profiles row exists.

277. Confirm interest row exists.

278. Confirm exactly one row exists in each required table.

279. Confirm Step 4 opens.

280. Log out.

281. Log in again.

282. Refresh.

283. Close and reopen.

284. Confirm session restoration.

285. Request password reset.

286. Receive the email.

287. Set a new password.

288. Confirm old password fails.

289. Confirm new password succeeds.

290. Confirm member cannot access owner routes.

291. Confirm owner can still access owner routes.

292. Confirm registration metrics increased correctly.

293. Clean up or mark the test user as QA.

294. Record the final trace IDs.

295. Record final screenshots.

==================================================
SECTION Q — FINAL ACCEPTANCE
==================================================

296. SMTP must be PASS.

297. Database constraints must be PASS.

298. Member signup must be PASS.

299. Email confirmation must be PASS.

300. Member sign-in must be PASS.

301. Owner sign-in must be PASS.

302. Password recovery must be PASS.

303. Session persistence must be PASS.

304. Role authorization must be PASS.

305. CloudFront assets must be current.

306. Samsung Browser must be tested.

307. Android Chrome must be tested.

308. iPhone Safari must be tested.

309. Desktop browser must be tested.

310. Duplicate prevention must be PASS.

311. Partial-account repair must be PASS.

312. Password and secrets must be absent from logs.

313. GitHub and runtime SHA must match.

314. Live canary must be PASS.

315. All critical automated tests must pass.

==================================================
